text:
Maya Patel: Quick — a candidate asked if they can roll over an old 401k into our plan during onboarding or if it has to wait until after payroll set up? Theyre asking because they want to consolidate before transferring funds.

Ethan Cole: We can accept rollovers at any time after the employee is active in BrightPlan. Practically payroll needs the account on file to start contributions. Rollover itself is done with the provider; it doesn't need to be tied to the first payroll.

Maya Patel: Ok cool. Any docs we should send them so they don't mess up tax treatment?

Jorge Ramirez: Send this checklist: 1) Contact old provider for a direct rollover (trustee-to-trustee). 2) Request BrightPlan rollover form (we have PDF link in Confluence). 3) Do not take distribution (taxable). I'll paste the internal link in a sec.

BenefitsBot: FYI: BrightPlan rollover form link: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/rollover.pdf (internal). Typical processing time: 7-14 business days.

Maya Patel: Awesome, I'll add that to the offer packet. Another question: does part-time (20-29 hrs/wk) get company match? Recruiting wants to be sure for hourly contractors transitioning to part-time.

Ethan Cole: Company match eligibility requires 20 hrs/week averaged over lookback period (per plan). If they meet eligibility, they get prorated employer match per payroll. We should confirm counted service with payroll for transfers from contractor->employee.

Olivia (Payroll): Confirmed: Payroll uses hours reported in their first 90 days to verify eligibility. For transfers from contractor, you need to set employee type to "new hire with contractor history" and attach contractor hours CSV. We can do a manual override if recruiting flags it.

Maya Patel: Great — is there an example CSV for the override?

Olivia (Payroll): Example:
```
employee_id,period_start,period_end,hours
E12345,2025-01-01,2025-01-15,72
E12345,2025-01-16,2025-01-31,80
```
Send to payroll@redwood.com with subject "401k hours override".

Jorge Ramirez: One more — candidate asked about Roth in-service conversions later. Can employees convert pre-tax balance to Roth in-plan?

Ethan Cole: The plan allows in-plan Roth conversions once per plan year; theres an after-tax tax liability. Recommend they speak to a tax advisor. BrightPlan has a conversion request flow.

BenefitsBot: Match reminder: 100% up to 3% + 50% next 2% (max 4%). Vesting: 25% after 1 year then monthly to 48 months.

Maya Patel: Helpful. I'll update the hiring docs: rollover link + CSV example + note on part-time match eligibility + Roth conversion caveat. Anything else?

Olivia (Payroll): Add note: first payroll cutoff for benefits elections is the Friday before start date. If they want contributions in first check, ensure offer is signed and payroll is set 10 days prior.

Maya Patel: Will do. Thanks! :tada:
